subject: Clarify DPA addendum: operator exception + subprocessor scope
messages:
From: Sam Keller <sam.keller@adriahealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: privacy@adriahealth.com
Date: Fri, 3 Oct 2025 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify DPA addendum — service provider scope and operator exception

Hi Grace,

Thanks for sending over the draft US addendum. Our legal team had two quick asks so we can move the contract forward: 1) confirm whether Redwood will accept a narrow operator exception for limited forwarding of telemetry to subcontractors under the same controller obligations, and 2) provide an up-to-date subprocessor list + attestation about onshore fallback for telemetry exports.

We've highlighted the clauses in the redline (attached) — the team is worried that the current language could be read as a broader "sale" or resale carve-out under CCPA/CPRA. If you can confirm that Redwood's role is limited to a service-provider-like handling for US-state privacy laws, and outline how subprocessors are controlled (esp. any onshore routing or fallback), that would help close this.

Ideal timeline: short call early next week and a clean addendum by end of week.

Thanks,
Sam Keller
VP, Platform Security
AdriaHealth

[Attachment: Adria_DPA_Redline_v1.docx (docx, 31 KB)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Keller <sam.keller@adriahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Oct 2025 17:10:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Clarify DPA addendum — service provider scope and operator exception

Jonas / Aditya — forwarding Adria's redline. Two asks below from legal: the operator exception question and a clear statement about subprocessors and onshore fallback.

Quick thoughts:
- We should avoid wording that uses the word "sale" or "resale" anywhere in the addendum. For CCPA/CPRA, "service provider" language plus a dedicated paragraph on handling of telemetry should be sufficient.
- For the operator exception, propose we offer a narrow carve: allow short-term, encrypted telemetry forwarding to select subprocessors for ops/debugging where Adria remains the controller of decisions about personal data, and Redwood acts solely as a conduit/processor. That keeps us in "service provider" posture.
- Subprocessor list: we'll send the current CSV and a short onshore-fallback note (how we route telemetry to US regions and fallback if a third-party region becomes unavailable).

Can you draft the compromise language we can send back? Sam is asking for an early-week call — can we offer Monday morning PDT?

Thanks,
Grace
Principal, Customer Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Keller <sam.keller@adriahealth.com>, privacy@adriahealth.com
Date: Mon, 6 Oct 2025 09:35:00 +0100
Subject: RE: Clarify DPA addendum — service provider scope and operator exception

Grace / Aditya — draft language below I think balances their ask without expanding legal exposure. I also attached a clean addendum we can send if you like.

Proposed narrow operator carve (suggested paragraph to add to addendum):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Addendum, Redwood may, solely for the purpose of providing support, debugging, or operational monitoring, transmit limited telemetry to a subcontractor where such transmission is strictly limited in scope and duration, subject to Redwood's contractual obligations to maintain the customer's processing instructions and not to retain or use Personal Information for any other purpose. Redwood shall ensure that any such subcontractor is bound by contractual terms consistent with this Addendum and shall provide Customer with notice and, upon request, evidence of onshore fallback measures for telemetry routing."

Subprocessor attachments posted: Draft_US_Addendum_v3.docx (redlines applied), subprocessor_list_20251003.csv (lists current subprocessors and region residency). I'm flagging two subprocessors that handle logging and metrics — both have US-based fallback and SOC2 evidence on file.

If Grace is happy, we can propose a 30-min call with Sam to walk through the paragraph and the fallback plan.

Jonas
Head of Privacy Ops
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Draft_US_Addendum_v3.docx (docx, 42 KB)]
[Attachment: subprocessor_list_20251003.csv (csv, 8 KB)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Keller <sam.keller@adriahealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, privacy@adriahealth.com
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Clarify DPA addendum — service provider scope and operator exception

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear redline and for raising the operator question. Per our internal review, Redwood can accept the narrow operator carve described below and has attached a cleaned addendum with that language inserted. Key points:

- Scope: the carve is explicitly limited to support/debugging/operational monitoring and only to telemetry necessary to diagnose/fix issues; it does not permit onward commercial use or behavioral profiling.
- Subprocessors: attached CSV lists current subprocessors; the two logging vendors have US-region fallbacks and we can provide SOC 2 artifacts on request.
- Notice & evidence: Redwood will provide 15 days' notice for any new subprocessors that would be used for telemetry and will provide onshore fallback attestation upon request within five business days.

If that sounds good, propose a 30-min call tomorrow (Wed 10/8) 9am PDT to confirm and then exchange a final executed addendum.

Thanks,
Grace
Principal, Customer Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
